prompt_text:
Task: Managed Object Storage

Write code that lists stored objects under a bucket or container prefix using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Azure Blob Storage:
  Service: Azure Blob Storage
  SDK: azure-storage-blob
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: upload_blob, get_blob_properties, generate_blob_sas
  Setup hints: AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_URL, AZURE_STORAGE_KEY
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/

Option 2 — Alibaba OSS:
  Service: Alibaba Object Storage Service
  SDK: oss2
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: put_object, sign_url, head_object
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/oss/

Option 3 — IBM Cloud Object Storage:
  Service: IBM Cloud Object Storage
  SDK: ibm-cos-sdk
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: upload_fileobj, generate_presigned_url, head_object
  Setup hints: IBM_COS_ENDPOINT, IBM_COS_APIKEY
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/cloud-object-storage

Option 4 — Google Cloud Storage:
  Service: Cloud Storage
  SDK: google-cloud-storage
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: upload_from_file, generate_signed_url, get_blob
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs

Option 5 — Amazon S3:
  Service: Amazon S3
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: put_object, generate_presigned_url, head_object
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/s3/

Option 6 — Backblaze B2:
  Service: Backblaze B2 Cloud Storage
  SDK: b2sdk
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: upload_local_file, download_file_by_name
  Setup hints: B2_APPLICATION_KEY_ID, B2_APPLICATION_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

output_text:
import os
from typing import List, Dict, Optional

from google.cloud import storage


def list_objects(bucket_name: str, prefix: str = "") -> List[Dict[str, object]]:
    """
    List stored objects in a Google Cloud Storage bucket under a given prefix.

    Requires:
        - google-cloud-storage
        - GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS set for authentication

    Returns:
        A list of dictionaries containing object metadata.
    """
    client = storage.Client()
    bucket = client.bucket(bucket_name)

    blobs = client.list_blobs(bucket, prefix=prefix)
    results: List[Dict[str, object]] = []

    for blob in blobs:
        results.append(
            {
                "name": blob.name,
                "bucket": blob.bucket.name,
                "size": blob.size,
                "content_type": blob.content_type,
                "updated": blob.updated.isoformat() if blob.updated else None,
                "created": blob.time_created.isoformat() if blob.time_created else None,
                "etag": blob.etag,
                "md5_hash": blob.md5_hash,
            }
        )

    return results


def _main() -> None:
    import argparse
    import json

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="List Google Cloud Storage objects by prefix.")
    parser.add_argument("bucket", help="GCS bucket name")
    parser.add_argument("--prefix", default="", help="Object prefix to filter by")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    objects = list_objects(args.bucket, args.prefix)
    print(json.dumps(objects, indent=2, sort_keys=True))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    _main()
